note: The golden-hour graph. Build six empty nodes on the reference clip once (Alt+S five times), run this, and the whole graph propagates to every clip on the timeline. Numbers live in the LUT at node 3; the other nodes are handles you turn by hand afterwards.

grades.name: golden hour graph, built on the reference clip

nodes.label: 01 BALANCE
nodes.note: Neutral on purpose. This is where a clip that drifted off the others gets pulled back — one clip at a time, in trims below.

nodes.label: 02 EXPOSURE
nodes.note: Backlit shots land dark. A touch of slope here, before the look, so the LUT gets the level it was designed for.

nodes.label: 03 LOOK
nodes.note: golden_hour.cube — the whole look. Everything above and below it is a handle.

nodes.label: 04 SKIN
nodes.note: The LUT adds saturation globally; this takes a little back so faces do not go orange under a sun that is already orange.

nodes.label: 05 SKY - window, add by hand
nodes.note: Off deliberately. A window or qualifier cannot be scripted, so this node is left empty and disabled: switch it on, draw a gradient across the sky, and it is already in the right place in the chain.

nodes.label: 06 TRIM
nodes.note: Neutral. The last word before output, for shot-to-shot matching.
